subject: LLM routing, regional sojourns, and export controls — residency & deletion Q&A
messages:
From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@nebulahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Residency question — where do LLM requests actually run?

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — Nebula is evaluating Redwood for a patient-facing feature. Before we move deeper the security and privacy team needs to confirm two things:

1) Where do inference requests originating from our US region get processed (regions, cloud providers, subprocessors)?
2) If traffic spikes and Redwood falls back to another region or model variant, how is cross-border transfer handled and logged?

Can you provide a concise summary and any evidence we can attach to our procurement packet (diagram or inventory is ideal)?

Best,
Sara
Sara Klein
Head of Product Security
Nebula Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency question — where do LLM requests actually run?

Sara — thanks for the clear ask. High level first, then I will loop in engineering for the exact evidence you requested (map + inventory).

High-level summary:
- Primary processing: Requests from US customers are routed to our US serving fleet (primary regions: us-east-1 and us-west-2). We prefer to keep inference processing within your chosen geographic scope.
- Subprocessors: Serving and control-plane components rely on cloud infra partners (AWS for serving, GCP for some batch jobs, and an object-storage subprocessor for user-managed artifacts). We will provide a snapshot inventory with roles and contact info.
- Fallbacks & cross-border behavior: By default, fallback routing is region-aware. If capacity is constrained and you have not opted into strict residency, requests may be routed to the next closest compatible region. All cross-border transfers are logged and surfaced in audit trails; we include request-level routing metadata (source region, served-region, model variant).

I will send a technical annex with: a diagram of request paths, a breakdown of subprocessors and their roles, and the exact logging fields you can reference. Marissa — I attached a one-page map (residency_map_v1.pdf) and the subprocessor snapshot; please confirm those are the latest exports and add anything Karthik should call out on technical controls.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Attachments: residency_map_v1.pdf

Subject: FW: Residency question — internal details + ask for Karthik on logs

Hannah / Karthik — forwarding Sara's note and Hannah's high-level reply. Quick notes:

- I refreshed the subprocessor export this morning (attached: subprocessor_inventory_snapshot.csv). It lists the roles (serving compute, control plane telemetry, object store for model artifacts) and the contracted regions for each supplier.
- Karthik, can you confirm the logging fields and retention? Specifically: routing.source_region, routing.serve_region, model_variant, request_id, and ttl for audit logs (we typically retain audit logs 1 year by default for hosted customers; can be extended under Dedicated/Private contracts).
- Also call out the opt-in flag customers use to lock residency (redwood.residency_enforcement = strict). If enabled, we guarantee served_region is within the selected geography and we will not route across borders for inference; that flows into the SLA/contract.

Marissa

Subject: RE: Residency question — where do LLM requests actually run? 

Sara — attaching the documents Marissa exported and Karthik's confirmations below. Thanks for the patient turnaround.

Short answers for your packet (copy/paste friendly):
- Regions & processing: Primary inference for Nebula Health (US tenancy) is served from our US fleet (us-east-1, us-west-2). For customers on Redwood Dedicated or Private we can pin a single AZ/region or provide an on-prem package to avoid cloud-region routing entirely.
- Subprocessors: Current serving infra is contracted with AWS (compute + networking) and a separate object-store subprocessor for model artifacts. Control-plane telemetry (usage metrics, analytics) may run in GCP for specific batch analytics jobs. The attached inventory identifies each subprocessor, role, legal entity, and contracting jurisdiction.
- Cross-border transfer & enforcement: By default (self-serve hosted) we attempt to keep traffic regional but allow geo-fallback to preserve availability; these events are logged. For strict residency guarantees you must enable redwood.residency_enforcement = strict or select Dedicated/Private; with enforcement enabled we will not route inference outside the chosen geography and transfers are disallowed by config and contract.
- Evidence & auditability: Audit logs (routing.*, request_id, served_region) are available via the Console and can be exported. We retain these logs for 12 months for hosted plans; retention can be extended contractually. All cross-border routing events surface a ticket and are included in monthly routing reports.

Attachments provided: residency_map_v1.pdf (diagram of request paths), subprocessor_inventory_snapshot.csv (vendor inventory).

If you need a signed attestation or a redlineable clause for the contract about residency enforcement, we can loop Legal / Contracts and provide tailored language (we have a standard residency exhibit used with several healthcare customers).

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
